comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted English Philosophy annual plan has ten required 6 EC first-year units, eight required and two selected 6 EC second-year units, and 30 EC of open study, two 6 EC philosophy choices, a 6 EC thesis seminar and a 12 EC thesis. The example selects Theoretical Philosophy and World Philosophies I in year two, and Contemporary Ethics and History of Philosophy in year three. The World Philosophies I/II condition is met once. Both first-year and second-year Philosophical Encounters seminars carry zero credits, as does the English language test. The test or completed refresher gates Academic English. The binding study recommendation requires 42 first-year EC and the language quality requirement. Political Philosophy includes a Broader Mind certificate. The thesis requires all first-year courses and 48 second-year EC, and is assessed by two readers. Open study has level, approval and non-overlap rules. The distinct Dutch Philosophy Plus routes do not enter this example.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two defensible options use philosophy as the taught subject, including six dedicated philosophy courses in each, complemented by legal philosophy and logic. The second option offers a distinct application in climate ethics and public reasoning. A mind-and-knowledge direction would rely on the same philosophy courses and shift toward empirical psychology if extended. The Dutch religion and governance variants do not establish additional routes within the English comparator.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: VU studies contemporary European philosophies in a dedicated course.
Both examine arguments from ancient Greek philosophy. VU also studies ancient traditions from South and East Asia.
VU compares medieval philosophical traditions across regions.
VU studies modern philosophical arguments in a dedicated course. UCR gives a broader historical introduction.
VU studies intercultural philosophy and postcolonial theory. UCR examines historical and cultural contexts across several courses.
VU traces the development of analytic philosophy through its texts and arguments.
VU compares how philosophical traditions are constructed. UCR studies selected perspectives within courses on mind, free will and culture.
VU’s elective studies Platonism and Neoplatonism in depth.
Both examine moral theories and apply ethical arguments to practical questions. UCR also develops an independent position through essays.
VU requires a dedicated Social Philosophy course. UCR considers social questions across ethics and political philosophy.
Both read political arguments and examine ideas about justice, power and society. VU also includes the Broader Mind course.
VU offers a specialist ethics elective. UCR applies normative reasoning across ethics, political philosophy and climate-related work.
VU examines theories of knowledge in a dedicated course.
Both study propositions, quantification and formal reasoning. UCR applies these tools to discrete mathematics, while VU also teaches natural deduction and philosophy of logic.
VU studies philosophical questions about scientific methods and explanation.
Both examine consciousness and the mind–body problem through philosophical arguments.
VU’s theoretical elective examines pragmatism in the published year.
Both examine free will, determinism and questions about time and personal identity. VU also studies other topics in contemporary metaphysics.
Both teach the analysis and construction of arguments. UCR applies this work to persuasive communication, while VU reconstructs and evaluates philosophical arguments.
VU devotes a seminar to close reading of Plato’s Sophist.
VU devotes a seminar to close reading of Kant’s Critique of Pure Reason.
VU teaches philosophical research and argument development in a dedicated thesis seminar.
VU requires a 12 EC individual philosophy thesis. Optional independent research at UCR sits outside the displayed schedules.
VU reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved elective study. UCR shows complete course schedules.
Both develop academic writing and use of sources. VU also teaches English grammar and requires a language test or refresher.

notes.text: VU devotes separate courses to global philosophical histories, epistemology and philosophy of science. It also requires close-reading seminars and an individual philosophy thesis. UCR develops philosophical arguments in ethics, mind, agency and political philosophy. Rhetoric in Action involves mainly Dutch interaction with local primary-school children. Independent research at UCR is optional and sits outside the displayed schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Philosophy studies historical, practical and theoretical philosophy. Students learn to evaluate arguments, read demanding texts closely and write an individual philosophy thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option combines philosophy with rhetoric and historical interpretation. The other applies ethics and political philosophy to climate responsibility, markets and public decisions.

curriculum.limitation: The English-track example includes 30 EC of open study and a 12 EC individual thesis. Thesis entry requires all first-year courses and 48 EC from year two. The language test or refresher is required for the Academic English grade.
